items.stem: Before letting the agent implement a feature, what single artefact most reduces the risk of building the wrong thing?

options.text: A plan stating the goal and acceptance criteria
options.rationale: Correct: explicit acceptance criteria define 'done' and guide the agent.

options.text: A longer prompt with more adjectives

options.rationale: More context does not substitute for a clear goal.

items.explanation: Correct: explicit acceptance criteria define 'done' and guide the agent.

items.stem: Which TWO practices keep agent-driven feature work reviewable? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Splitting the feature into small, testable increments
options.rationale: Correct: small increments are easier to review and verify.
Correct: per-increment testing catches regressions early.

options.text: Making one sweeping change at the end
options.rationale: Large opaque changes are hard to review.

options.text: Skipping review when the feature appears to work
options.rationale: Appearance of working is not verification.

items.explanation: Correct: small increments are easier to review and verify.

items.stem: Mid-task, the agent starts refactoring unrelated modules not in the plan. The best response is to:

options.text: Stop, roll back the drift, and resume from the last good checkpoint
options.rationale: Correct: halting drift and resuming from a known-good point protects the work.

options.text: Let it continue since more refactoring is good
options.rationale: Unplanned sweeping changes increase risk and review burden.
Accepting unreviewed drift defeats the plan.
A rollback to checkpoint is sufficient and less destructive.

items.explanation: Correct: halting drift and resuming from a known-good point protects the work.
